body.statement: For the balanced experiment with \(K=3\), \(N=6\), \(n=2\), \(m=1\), \(C=(1,1,-2)\), and \(W=(1)\), \[H=C^{\mathsf T}WC=\begin{pmatrix}1&1&-2\\1&1&-2\\-2&-2&4\end{pmatrix}\notin\mathcal R_3\] because \(H_{12}=1>0\). Let \(F_1=F_2=\tfrac12\delta_0+\tfrac12\delta_1\) and \(F_3=\delta_0\). Common ranking uses columns \((0,0,0,1,1,1)^{\mathsf T}\), \((0,0,0,1,1,1)^{\mathsf T}\), and zero, so \(S_{11}=S_{22}=S_{12}=3/10\) and \(\rho_W\{Y^{\uparrow}(F)\}=1/10\). Reversing only the second binary column gives a feasible \(Y\) with \(S_{11}=S_{22}=3/10\), \(S_{12}=-3/10\), and \(\rho_W(Y)=3/10\). Consequently \[\rho_W\{Y^{\uparrow}(F)\}-\rho_W(Y)=\frac{1}{3}(-1)\left\{\frac{3}{10}-\left(-\frac{3}{10}\right)\right\}=-\frac{1}{5},\] an exact binary certificate of strict common-rank failure.
body.justification: The witness exposes the necessity mechanism with a valid contrast Gram matrix, isolated binary margins, and exact finite-sample losses.
body.gap: Classical rearrangement results imply how a signed pair behaves but do not identify this non-Laplacian causal contrast or evaluate its complete-randomization loss.
body.consumer: Software checking \(H_{ab}\leq0\) can return this exact three-arm counterexample template whenever it detects a positive off-diagonal coefficient.
